headline: ASX 200 female board representation rose from 8.7% in 2010 to 30% in 2020; ~60% of surveyed boards now exceed 40% women, but ~70% of roles still filled via informal networks
reasoning: Ruth Medd noted that measurable progress has been made on gender diversity in Australian boardrooms over two decades, with ASX 200 female representation growing from 8.7% in 2010 to 30% in 2020. She also noted that approximately 60% of boards in Women on Boards' survey group now have more than 40% women. However, she flagged that only around 30% of board roles are advertised more widely or sent to headhunters, with the remainder filled through informal 'who you know' networks. She advocates for explicit diversity targets, drawing an analogy to other business KPIs such as profit targets and staff retention rates. The 40-40-20 gender balance model is the framework she champions for boards going forward.
quote: So in 2010, for example, the ASX 200 had 8.7% women on it and in 2020 it had 30%. So and all the sectors that we measured improved over time. And these days about 60% of the boards that are in this survey group have got more than 40% women. So that's a pretty solid achievement from a starting point where nobody bothered to actually measure it or count it... it's still the case that, I mean the figures are a bit dodgy, but perhaps 30 ish percent of roles are now advertised more widely or sent to the headhunters and the rest of them sort of who you know now.
episode_title: 20 years of Women On Boards... has much changed?
